title: weak null singularities for the einstein--vlasov system
abstract: we study the formation and stability of weak null singularities for solutions to the massive and massless einstein--vlasov systems without symmetry assumptions. extending previous results of luk in the vacuum setting, we establish the existence of spacetimes arising from characteristic initial data that develop a singular null boundary while remaining extendible with a continuous metric. for both massive and massless particles, the energy-momentum tensor and ricci curvature remain bounded and extend continuously to the singular boundary. for genuinely singular initial data, the christoffel symbols in the original double-null coordinates fail to be locally square integrable near the boundary. we introduce new commutator vector fields that avoid both derivative loss and the most singular curvature component. under additional curvature assumptions, we also prove lipschitz inextendibility across the singular null boundary.

title: the uniqueness of smooth stationary black holes
abstract: we show that the domain of outer communications of a smooth, asymptotically flat, stationary vacuum spacetime describing a single rotating non-degenerate black hole is isometric to the domain of outer communications of a subextremal kerr solution under reasonable geometric and physical assumptions, without analyticity or any smallness assumptions. the method is to apply harrison transform to construct a family of solutions of einstein--maxwell equations. combining null area comparison with the area-charge inequality, we show that, in the limiting transformed geometry, the bifurcate sphere has area radius one and constant electric and magnetic flux densities, with the original adm mass normalized to $m=1$. these identities imply the technical assumptions of ionescu--klainerman, yielding the identification with kerr.

title: conformal boundary rigidity from null geodesic travel times
abstract: the gravitational field of a distant, isolated system is manifested by the conformally invariant weyl tensor. thus the conformal structure far from the system encodes the system's gravitational mass. it also encodes the causal structure, thereby linking it to the mass. for asymptotically anti-de sitter (ads) spacetimes, this link led to a novel positive mass theorem of page, surya, and the second author \cite{psw} which did not rely on any traditional energy condition. here we ask whether that theorem has a rigidity case. specifically, we consider all null geodesics in an asymptotically ads spacetime that depart from the penrose conformal infinity, travel through spacetime, and return to conformal infinity. if all such geodesics from a given point refocus at an antipodal point at infinity, is the spacetime conformal to anti-de sitter space? it is easy to answer the question if the asymptotically ads spacetime either (i) obeys the null energy condition in 3 or 4 spacetime dimensions, or (ii) is static (in any dimension), and we give simple proofs in those cases. we then answer the question in the case of globally stationary, asymptotically ads spacetimes, by applying the theory of magnetic geodesics on the riemannian manifold-with-boundary obtained by quotienting by the stationary killing vector field. the question has an analogue for asymptotically flat spacetimes, which we also discuss.

title: exact model of a gravitational wave and electromagnetic radiation in dhost gravity theory: wave solutions and testable effects
abstract: within an analytical non-perturbative framework based on a single exact model, the coupled dynamics of gravitational waves and high-frequency electromagnetic fields is investigated in general relativity and dhost gravity. using an exact gravitational-wave spacetime in an isotropic (null) wave coordinate system, maxwell's equations are integrated analytically. this analysis provides an exact non-perturbative confirmation from the full field equations that a gravitational wave acts as a waveguide, forming a propagation channel for electromagnetic radiation co-directional with the gravitational wave and generating an effective pure-radiation source. applying this exact electrodynamic solution to the nonlinear field equations of dhost class~ia gravity reveals that the algebraic structure of the dhost constraint equations enforces a modification of the electromagnetic-wave parameters. based on this mechanism, an observationally testable effect of scalar frequency drift is derived, providing a direct way to discriminate between general relativity and modified gravity theories even when their metric tensors share identical functional forms.

title: entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in schwarzschild spacetime
abstract: we prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended schwarzschild spacetime. as a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. as a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended schwarzschild, which is cauchy and has properties of independent interest.

title: machine learning and high accuracy: neural preconditioners for computational gravity
abstract: machine learning (ml) developments have empowered valuable calculations in many areas of theoretical physics. certain topics involving moderate-to-low accuracy requirements have been particularly fortunate because many ml techniques, such as neural networks, introduce a noise floor that would be difficult to penetrate with stricter tolerances. for this reason, topics requiring high accuracy can be hesitant to pursue ml. one prominent example is gravitational wave modeling, which relies on traditional methods that accommodate the high sensitivities of detectors such as lisa. however, recent progress in applied mathematics has identified hybrid methods where fast-but-noisy ml mechanisms are inserted into otherwise traditional numerical schemes to accelerate convergence in a way that ultimately meets or exceeds the accuracy of standard methods. we develop an optimized hybrid ml method to tackle a class of challenging pdes; specifically, we demonstrate ml implementations for gravitational waves from asymmetric-mass black hole binaries and elastic waves. these require solving sparse linear algebra systems with helmholtz features that are especially difficult for traditional iterative methods. our new approach is to train a graph neural network (gnn) as a significantly faster preconditioner using a novel loss function based on the true residual of the iterative algorithm. for the most difficult regions of parameter space, our neural preconditioner decreases iteration counts by 2-15x compared to traditional preconditioners. because the gnn operates directly on the sparse matrix and needs only modest physical context, it generalizes beyond its training domain and can be adapted to new problems across physics by retraining rather than redesign. hybrid ml methods such as this offer a new and compelling avenue to handle high accuracy and speed requirements in gravitational wave modeling and beyond.

title: the cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity
abstract: we solve the cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the cauchy hypersurface $σ$. we characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. in particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional neveu-schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. this establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric neveu-schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric neveu-schwarz solution with a compact cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.

title: electromagnetic scattering by minkowski-type bianisotropic media
abstract: we consider the time-harmonic scattering of electromagnetic waves by a bounded stationary inclusion whose effective constitutive law is of minkowski type. the constant vector $v$ is regarded as a constitutive moving parameter. such a law arises as an effective description of synthetic moving media and of suitable traveling-wave space--time modulations. starting from the implicit minkowski relations, we derive a maxwell transmission system and its lippmann--schwinger volume-integral formulation. the dimensionless parameter $β=|v|/c_ω$ governs the pointwise constitutive inversion, namely the matrix is invertible precisely for $β\neq1$, while on the subcritical branch $0\leqβ<1$ its inverse admits an explicit convergent expansion. using the algebraic structure of the cross-product operator, we obtain a spectral characterization of solvability and a quantitative sufficient condition separating the static material contrast from the $v$-dependent contribution which allows to justify the convergence of the corresponding born series. as an application, we prove that full-aperture electric far-field data at a fixed frequency uniquely determine the support of the inclusion within this perturbative regime without assuming that $v$ is known.

title: boundary value problems for 0-elliptic operators
abstract: let $x$ be a manifold with boundary, and let $l$ be a 0-elliptic operator on x which is semi-fredholm essentially surjective with infinite-dimensional kernel. examples include hodge laplacians and dirac operators on conformally compact manifolds. we construct left and right parametrices for l when supplemented with appropriate elliptic boundary conditions. the construction relies on a new calculus of pseudodifferential operators on functions over both $x$ and $\partial x$, which we call the "symbolic 0-calculus". this new calculus supplements the ordinary 0-calculus of mazzeo--melrose, enabling it to handle boundary value problems. in the original 0-calculus, operators are characterized as polyhomogeneous right densities on a blow-up of $x^2$. by contrast, operators in the symbolic 0-calculus are characterized (locally near each point of the boundary of the diagonal) as quantizations of polyhomogeneous symbols on appropriate blown-up model spaces.

title: spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $l_p$ minkowski problem
abstract: we investigate the isotropic $l_p$ minkowski problem in $\mathbb{r}^n$ for $p<-n$. we prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $k$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the hilbert-brunn-minkowski operator satisfies $λ_2(-l_k)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. we also derive a lower bound for $λ_2(-l_k)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.

title: heat kernel estimates for markov processes with blowing-up jump kernels
abstract: in this paper, we establish sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for a large class of purely discontinuous symmetric markov processes on closed subsets $f$ of $\mathbb{r}^d$, whose jump kernels blow up on a borel subset $σ$ of $f$. we assume that $f\setminus σ$ is a $κ$-fat set and is dense in $f$, and additionally, in case of unbounded $f$, that the assouad dimension of $f$ is strictly less than $d$. to the best of our knowledge, this is the first work establishing sharp two-sided heat kernel estimates for jump processes whose jump kernels blow up on part of the state space. the jump kernels under consideration take the form $j(x,y)=|x-y|^{-d-α}{\mathcal b}(x,y)$, where $α\in (0,2)$ and the function ${\mathcal b}(x,y)$ blows up at a subset $σ$ of $f$. a fundamental obstacle is that the tails of the jump measures are not uniformly bounded, and hence standard techniques in heat kernel analysis do not provide a priori off-diagonal estimates. to overcome this difficulty, we develop a new approach based on weighted integral estimates for the heat kernel that are sensitive to both the blow-up behavior of the jump kernel and the geometry of $f\setminus σ$. examples of processes falling within our general framework include traces of isotropic $α$-stable processes in some unbounded $c^{1,\rm dini}$ sets, processes in lipschitz sets arising in connection with the nonlocal neumann problem, and a large class of resurrected self-similar processes in the closed upper half-space.

title: bilinear embedding for divergence-form operators with first-order terms and negative potentials
abstract: this article establishes a bilinear embedding for second-order divergence-form operators with complex coefficients, characterized by the simultaneous presence of first-order terms and negative potentials. this work provides a further development of the theory initiated by carbonaro and dragičević for the homogeneous case, and recently extended by the second author in two papers where first-order terms and negative potentials were treated separately. we work in the general setting of arbitrary open subsets of $\mathbb{r}^d$ under dirichlet, neumann, or mixed boundary conditions. our main contribution is the introduction of a unified notion of generalized $p$-ellipticity that extends all its predecessors and serves as the natural condition for the bilinear inequality. methodologically, we overcome the rigidity of the bellman-heat method on arbitrary open subsets by introducing a novel sequence-based approach that unifies and simplifies the previous techniques. as fundamental applications, we prove the boundedness of the $h^\infty$-calculus on $l^p$ and establish $l^p$-maximal regularity. moreover, we show that this generalized $p$-ellipticity provides a sufficient condition for the $l^p$-contractivity and $l^p$-analyticity of the generated semigroup. finally, we apply our theory to magnetic schrödinger operators, characterizing the range of exponents $p$ for which the associated coefficient tuple satisfies the generalized $p$-ellipticity condition introduced here.

title: refined asymptotic estimates, morse index and nondegeneracy of solutions to a biharmonic problem with large exponents in dimension four
abstract: we are concerned with the semilinear biharmonic problem under dirichlet boundary conditions \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} δ^2 u=(u^+)^{p} &{\text{in}~ω},\\[0.5mm]   u \not\equiv 0 &{\text{in}~ω},\\[0.5mm] u=\dfrac{\partial u}{\partial ν} = 0 &{\text{on}~\partial ω}, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $ω\subset \mathbb{r}^4$ is a smooth bounded domain, $u^+ = \max\{u,0\}$, $ν$ denotes the outward unit normal and $p>1$ is sufficiently large. the basic concentration behavior of solutions satisfying the uniform energy bound is known. in this work, we first obtain refined asymptotic estimates for the peak heights, concentration scales and rescaled profiles of multi-spike solutions. based on these estimates, we further analyze the generalized linearized eigenvalue problem and derive sharp bounds for the morse and augmented morse indices. consequently, if the limiting $k$-spike configuration ${\mathbf{x}}_\infty$ is a nondegenerate critical point of kirchhoff--routh function $ψ_k$, then \[ m(u_p)=k+n_+\big(d^2ψ_k({\mathbf{x}}_\infty)\big) \] and $u_p$ is nondegenerate for all sufficiently large $p$ along the selected concentration subsequence. the absence of the maximum principle for the dirichlet biharmonic operator on general domains poses main difficulties in both refined asymptotic analysis and the study of the generalized linearized eigenvalue problem. to address these difficulties, we employ green's representation together with refined blow-up and spectral analysis.

title: global existence, blow-up behavior and numerical simulations for a class of chemotaxis-driven fish-mussel systems
abstract: in this work, we investigate a chemotaxis-driven fish--mussel ecosystem model described by a coupled system of partial differential equations subject to homogeneous neumann boundary conditions. under suitable assumptions on the system parameters and initial data, we establish the global existence of classical solutions by employing semigroup methods together with a priori estimates. we also examine the possible blow-up behavior of solutions in a three-dimensional domain. to support the theoretical analysis, a finite element method is developed for the numerical approximation of the system, and convergence studies based on mesh refinement are carried out to verify the accuracy and stability of the proposed numerical scheme. furthermore, numerical simulations illustrating the blow-up behavior of solutions in the computational domain are presented.

title: finite-time singularities of lagrangian mean curvature flow with quantitatively precise dynamics
abstract: for each integer $k\geq2$ when $n\geq4$, and for $k=2,3,4$ when $n=3$, we construct an almost-calibrated lagrangian mean curvature flow $l_k(t)$ in $\mathbb{c}^{n}$, starting from initial data arbitrarily close to being special lagrangian, which develops a finite-time type ii singularity at time $t$ with the explicit curvature blow up rate \[   \sup_{l_{k}(t)} |\mathbf{a}_{l_{k}(t)}| \sim (t-t)^{-k/2}   \qquad \text{as } t\nearrow t . \] the tangent flow at the singularity is a transverse pair of cohomogeneity-one special lagrangian cones, while the type ii blow-up limit is a smooth cohomogeneity-one special lagrangian desingularization.   this gives a quantitative construction of type ii blow-up for a fully nonlinear parabolic pde arising from cohomogeneity-one lagrangian mean curvature flow. our construction is based on a modulation analysis around a shrinking family of cohomogeneity-one special lagrangian desingularizations, using the perturbative spectral theory developed in the companion paper.

title: small-data $l^2$ theory for the intermediate nls and the calogero--moser derivative nls
abstract: in this paper, we study a class of nonlinear schrödinger equations (nls) in a unified way. this class includes two important examples: the intermediate nls (inls) and the calogero--moser derivative nls (cm-dnls). our main results are twofold. first, we prove small-data global well-posedness in $l^2(\mathbb{r})$ for a broad class of equations. this includes both focusing and defocusing cm-dnls and the inls for arbitrary choices of its parameters. second, we prove small-data scattering in $l^2(\mathbb{r})$ under an additional assumption. this result covers both focusing and defocusing cm-dnls and the inls for specific choices of its parameters. both the formulation of the problem, including the notion of solution, and the proofs rely crucially on a linear theory for schrödinger equations with rough time-dependent potentials. this theory is also of independent interest, since we allow potentials so rough that the standard duhamel formulation may not make sense. our approach is perturbative and is built on the bilinear strichartz estimate proved by ozawa and tsutsumi in 1998. in particular, our argument does not rely on integrability.

title: damped wave equation with a dynamic boundary condition: sharp resolvent estimate
abstract: this work investigates the stabilization of a wave equation with a localized damping and dynamic boundary conditions. this model traces back to the classical treatment of torsion and impact problems. consider a second-order hyperbolic equation posed with a dynamic boundary condition on a smooth compact riemannian manifold $(\m,g)$ with boundary, in which the damping acts either in the interior or on $\d \m$. under the assumption that the damping is positive on an open subset of its domain of action, a resolvent estimate is established. a logarithmic decay rate is then deduced for the energy of strong solutions. we provide examples that establish the sharpness of the resolvent estimate.

title: diffusion phenomena for evolution equations
abstract: we study the diffusion phenomenon for the abstract damped wave equation $u''+bu'+au=0$ on a banach space and its possibly degenerate parabolic counterpart $bv'+av=0$. we assume that $b$ is bounded and the wave equation is well-posed, without requiring symmetry, injectivity, or commutativity of $a$ and $b$. our aim is to identify initial data for which the parabolic solution is a genuine diffusive profile: $\|u(t)-v(t)\|=o(\|v(t)\|)$ as $t\to\infty$.   using fourier analysis of resolvent expressions for the associated quadratic and linear operator pencils, we establish decay estimates for the difference of hyperbolic and parabolic solutions and their time derivatives. in particular, we characterize broad classes of initial data yielding the classical upper bounds of orders $t^{-1}$ and $t^{-2}$. we also prove lower bounds for both solutions, of the form $\|u(t)\|,\|v(t)\|\gtrsim r(t)$, for large sets of initial data and arbitrary prescribed functions $r(t)\to0$ that decay sufficiently slowly. combining these results with high- and low-frequency resolvent estimates and a condition on the ranges of $a$ and $b$, we obtain genuine diffusive profiles. the analysis uses spectral properties of a sectorially holomorphic parabolic solution semigroup, which need not be strongly continuous.   we apply the theory to damped wave equations on $l^2(ω)$ with the dirichlet laplacian and bounded nonnegative damping that may vanish on large sets. we establish criteria for the required resolvent and range conditions, treat the whole space and exterior domains, and construct diffusive initial data using weyl sequences.

title: remarks on the bkm criterion for both classical and variable euler systems
abstract: in this paper, we establish new results on bkm-type criteria for the incompressible euler equations on $\mathbb{r}^3$ as well as the euler equations with space-time variable coefficients in a bounded domain. our first result shows that if a finite-energy solution to the euler equations on $\mathbb{r}^3$ blows up at a time $t_\ast$, and $t_\ast$ is the first such time, then $\limsup_{t\to t_\ast^-}(t_\ast -t)^{1+2k/5}\|d^kω(t)\|_{l^\infty} = \infty$ for every $k \geq 1$, thereby excluding the endpoint rate allowed by previously established lower bounds. the proof assumes the endpoint rate as an upper bound near the blowup time and uses a result by chae and wolf to obtain a contradiction. the second result gives a bkm-type criterion for solutions to the incompressible euler equations with variable coefficients in the minimal regularity class $h^r$, where $r \in (2.5,3)$.

title: self-similar cusp formation in a large class of nonlocal transport equations
abstract: we prove finite-time gradient blow-up with sharp $c^{(5-b)/(b+3)}$ hölder regularity for a class of nonlocal transport equations extending the $b$-family, for all real $1<b<5$. this class includes the camassa--holm and degasperis--procesi equations and, after rescaling, the generalized hyperelastic-rod wave equation. in the blow-up regime, the nonlocal equations reduce at leading order to the generalized hunter--saxton (ghs) equation with parameter $\ell=2/(b-1)$, whose self-similar scaling and corresponding profiles depend on $\ell$. consequently, standard approaches tailored to a fixed self-similar profile cannot be applied directly. to handle this parameter dependence, we develop a general framework for self-similar singularity formation in evolution equations whose leading-order dynamics are governed by the ghs family. the key ingredient is a family of profile inequalities established for all real $\ell>1/2$, which we combine with a generalized maximum principle to close a parameter-dependent bootstrap argument. we identify model-specific hypotheses adapted to this framework, under which this argument yields the required stability estimates. this leads to a general theorem on singularity formation, which we apply to the entire class of nonlocal equations, thereby establishing finite-time gradient blow-up and sharp hölder regularity. the theorem can also be applied to other evolution equations once the corresponding model-specific hypotheses are verified, without repeating the profile analysis or the common stability argument.

title: determination of a bi-periodic refractive index for the helmholtz equation
abstract: we investigate an inverse problem for the helmholtz equation in a three-dimensional half-space with a biperiodic medium above a sound-soft plane. we establish the uniqueness of a real-valued, bounded, biperiodic refractive index that depends only on the horizontal variables using spectral techniques. %the frequency and quasiperiodicity parameter are fixed. an orthogonality identity is first derived from near-field measurements. by constructing suitable separated solutions, this identity is reduced to relations involving eigenfunctions of two-dimensional quasiperiodic schrödinger operators. to recover fourier information from these relations, we project horizontal plane waves onto suitable high-energy spectral subspaces, obtaining finite combinations of eigenfunctions that approximate the plane waves with a quantified error. combining these approximations with the orthogonality identity, we show that all fourier coefficients of the difference of two refractive indices vanish, thereby establishing the desired uniqueness.

title: blow-up rate for 1-d semilinear wave equations without scaling invariance at characteristic points
abstract: we investigate the blow-up behavior of solutions to the semilinear wave equation $$ \partial_t^2 u - \partial_x^2 u = |u|^{p-1}u \ln^a(u^2+2), \quad (x,t)\in \mathbb{r} \times [0,t), $$ with $p > 1$ and $a<0$. while the blow-up rate at non-characteristic points was determined for all $a \in \mathbb{r}$ in previous work, the analysis at characteristic points has remained an open problem. the main obstruction is that known constructions of a lyapunov functional in similarity variables require several steps and rely on a covering argument, which is not available at characteristic points. focusing on the regime $a < 0$, we construct a lyapunov functional directly, without any covering argument. this yields uniform bounds on the solution in similarity variables, and hence the blow-up rate at every point, including characteristic ones. to our knowledge, this is the first work to determine the blow-up rate at characteristic points for an equation without scaling invariance.

title: evolution of internal waves on surfaces of revolution with flat ends
abstract: we generalize the 2d linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. we show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. this is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.

title: critical mass for infinite-time blow-up in a keller-segel system with indirect signal production on closed riemannian surfaces
abstract: we study a parabolic-elliptic-ode chemotaxis system with indirect signal production on closed connected riemannian surfaces. for all sufficiently regular nonnegative initial data, the system admits a unique global classical solution. we show that the solution remains globally bounded if the total mass $m<8π$. for each $m>8π$, we find initial data of mass $m$ that yield infinite-time blow-up solutions. we then adapt the argument to the corresponding neumann problem in a smooth bounded planar domain and obtain infinite-time blow-up solutions for any mass $m>4π$. at the critical mass $m=8π$, we show that the solutions are globally bounded on spheres equipped with the canonical spherical metric, and we construct a solution blowing up in infinite time on the riemann sphere equipped with a special metric.

title: asymptotic stability of self-similar blow-up for the two-dimensional zakharov system
abstract: we prove asymptotic stability of the small-parameter glangetas-merle self-similar blow-up solutions of the two-dimensional zakharov system under nonradial perturbations in the energy space. the proof establishes dissipation on the wave time scale by canceling the fast density coupling. we impose nonlinear orthogonality to the ground state of the density-dependent schrödinger operator for modulation and use successive energy corrections after subtracting the instantaneous density response from the schrödinger error. the resulting dissipation yields power-law decay of the rescaled errors in the schrödinger gradient, weighted local mass, and wave energy norms.

title: cavity collapse and vorticity gradient blow-up in free-boundary euler flow
abstract: we construct smooth solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary euler equations with surface tension whose vorticity remains bounded while its full spatial gradient blows up in finite time. the solutions are axisymmetric without swirl and occupy bounded domains in which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at time $t$, while the outer free surface converges smoothly. the vorticity $ω$ can be chosen arbitrarily small in $l^\infty$, uniformly up to collapse, and satisfies $\|\nablaω(t)\|_{l^\infty}\asymp (t-t)^{-1/2}|\log(t-t)|^{1/4}$ as $t\uparrow t$. a nonconstant material trace of the relative vorticity on the shrinking surface determines direction-dependent limits of the terminal vorticity, which therefore has no continuous extension across the collapse circle. the kinetic energy measure converges to the sum of a uniform line measure on this circle and a nonzero bulk part carried by a bounded rotational field. the construction couples vorticity transport to the boundary dynamics through weighted estimates in the collapsing collar and a cancellation in the normal acceleration.

title: discrete unique continuation for schrödinger equations
abstract: we study discrete unique continuation for one-dimensional schrödinger equations. we prove that if a solution vanishes at the points $\pm n^α$ at time $0$ and at the points $\pm n^β$ at time $1$, it must vanish identically in two main cases: the case of a schrödinger equation with a real potential that is uniformly of gevrey class $σ\ge 0$ in space, provided that $\max\{1,σ\}\big(α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)\big)<1$, and in the case of the cubic nonlinear schrödinger equation, provided that $α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)<1$.   unlike previous results for logarithmically spaced zeros, our methods do not rely on complex analysis. we first show that, whenever $α+β<1$, the zeros force the solution to lie in the schwartz class at all times. we then convert the zeros into gaussian decay at the two times, by combining energy estimates for iterations of the vector field $γ=x+2it\partial_x$ with techniques from fourier uniqueness problems, and conclude with the morgan-type uncertainty principle of escauriaza, kenig, ponce and vega.

title: radiation and persistent shape dynamics for the five-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear wave equation
abstract: we consider the nonradial five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. we construct a forward-global solution which remains arbitrarily close to a nondegenerate sign-changing stationary state in the energy space and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. the stationary profile moves in a compact conformal family, but its limit set contains a continuum of classes modulo translations, dilations and rotations. consequently, the solution admits no soliton resolution using a fixed finite collection of stationary profiles and fixed lorentz velocities, with pairwise orthogonal spatial parameters. that is, we disprove the fixed-profile soliton resolution conjecture for the five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. the construction uses a sequence of incoming waves with summable energies. their quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. the main estimates control the zero eigenvalue of the linearized operator and the nonlinear error uniformly over the entire sequence. the stationary input uses a computer-assisted spectral bound for a symmetric single-node state.

title: a counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
abstract: we consider the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. we construct a bounded forward-global solution which starts arbitrarily close to a sign-changing stationary state and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. the core has two limits in distinct similarity orbits. a single energy-space norm identity identifies the radiation and reduces every competing fixed list to one profile; the two limits then give a contradiction. the construction uses summable radiation packets whose quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. we control the nonlinear error uniformly over these intervals and select the endpoints by a compact fixed-point map. a computer-assisted certificate validates the stationary state and its complete odd energy kernel.

title: thermality from a rindler quench
abstract: ultracold fermionic atoms in an optical lattice, with a sudden position-dependent change (a quench) in the effective dispersion relation, have been proposed by rodríguez-laguna et al. as an analogue spacetime test of the unruh effect. we provide new support for this analogue by analysing a massless scalar field on a $(1+1)$-dimensional continuum spacetime with a similar quench: an early time minkowski region is joined at a constant time surface, representing the quench, to a late time static region in which left and right asymptotically rindler domains are connected by a smooth negative curvature bridge. we show that the quench is energetically mild, and late time static observers, modelled as a derivative-coupling unruh-dewitt detector, see thermality, in a temperature that equals the unruh temperature for observers in the asymptotic rindler domains. the unruh effect hence prevails, despite the energy injected into the field by the quench and despite the absence of a late time killing horizon. these results strengthen the motivation to realise the experimental proposal.

title: polarized image of synchrotron radiations of hotspots in schwarzschilld-melvin black hole spacetime
abstract: we revisit the innermost stable circular orbits (iscos) of charged particles and study the polarized images of synchrotron radiations emitted from such orbiting hotspots on the equatorial plane in {schwarzschild}-melvin black hole spacetime. we obtain a constraint on the magnetic field for the existence of charged-particle circular orbits. in particular, we identify a critical value for the strength of the magnetic field $b_c$ that the circular orbits can have positive and negative angular momentums {below} $b_c$ while only the negative angular momentum branch survives above} $b_c$. furthermore, we investigate and discuss the primary and secondary images of circularly orbiting charged hotspots carrying the information of polarization directions observed by distant observers. {we also find that the observed polarization angle varies rapidly with source azimuth when the emitted photon direction is nearly aligned with the local magnetic field, and explain the origin of this behavior.

title: popcorn emris: transient gravitational wave signals and their analysis in schwartz space
abstract: this study investigates extreme-mass ratio inspirals (emris) with orbital periods exceeding the observation windows of mhz gravitational wave detectors. during their early, highly eccentric stages, these systems produce periodic gravitational wave eruptions at pericentre, separated by long quiescent periods. we define these systems as ``popcorn emris''--bound, coherent binaries in a deterministic evolutionary phase. this distinguishes them from stochastic, non-coherent bursts associated with parabolic fly-bys. using a steady-state model based on the phase-space continuity equation, we estimate the population within a milky way-like galaxy. because these estimates depend on sensitive astrophysical variables like stellar relaxation and density profiles, our figures are illustrative rather than absolute. for a one-year observation baseline, we estimate a steady-state population of 200 to 2,000 popcorn emris, significantly outnumbering the 10 to 88 continuously observable emris. this yields an expected rate of 5 to 44 detectable eruptions per year. despite high signal-to-noise ratios (exceeding 700 for galactic centre events), the low duty cycle confirms their transient nature. standard data processing techniques, designed for continuous signals, often employ windowing that distorts eruption morphology and artificially reduces the signal-to-noise ratio. to address this, we establish a mathematical apparatus using based on standard smoothing techniques, in the theory of tempered distributions. we demonstrate that standard windowing techniques irreversibly degrade the signal-to-noise ratio of transient sources when the taper overlaps the eruption, and we utilize schwartz space regularization to justify the direct fourier transform as the energy-preserving estimator.

title: chaotic dynamics around a hairy black hole in horndeski gravity
abstract: we investigate the chaotic dynamics of a spinning test particle in a static, spherically symmet- ric hairy black hole (bh) in horndeski gravity, using the mathisson-papapetrou-dixon equations closed by the tulczyjew-dixon condition. bound orbits are identified by fixing the angular momen- tum and setting the energy according to the effective potential, so that the accessible parameter range is bounded by a critical hair parameter, hcrit, which varies non-monotonically with the spin. we analyze the resulting chaotic behavior using lyapunov exponents, poincare sections, and re- constructed attractors. we find that the response of these indicators to scalar hair is orbit- and spin-dependent rather than universally monotonic. an analysis of orbital frequency ratios shows that, at physically maximal spin (s = 1), an approaching 2:1 azimuthal resonance overlapping a persistent 1:1 polar lock amplifies chaos, while the hair-driven erosion of potential saddles tends to suppress it. at non-physical spin (s = 1.5), the lyapunov exponent decreases monotonically. gravitational waveforms constructed via the quadrupole formula inherit the same state-specific pattern: the correlation between the two polarization modes varies non-monotonically with h, in step with the lyapunov exponent. these results show that chaotic indicators respond to scalar hair in an orbit- and resonance-dependent manner rather than through simple monotonic suppres- sion, and identify the spin-dependent resonance structure as an essential ingredient for interpreting chaos around hairy black holes.

title: periodic orbits and gravitational waveforms of spinning particles in nonlocal gravity
abstract: in this paper, we investigate the dynamics and gravitational-wave signatures of periodic orbits of spinning test particles moving in the equatorial plane around static, spherically symmetric black holes within the framework of deser-woodard nonlocal gravity. based on the mathisson-papapetrou-dixon equations, combined with the tulczyjew spin supplementary condition, we derive the orbital dynamic equations for spinning particles moving in the equatorial plane and impose a timelike constraint to exclude unphysical superluminal trajectories. by comparing with the classical schwarzschild black hole, we systematically analyze the effects of the nonlocal gravitational parameters $ζ$ and $b$ on the effective potential governing the radial motion of particles and the innermost stable circular orbit. in addition, gravitational waveforms exhibit significant phase differences: an increase in $ζ$ induces a phase delay, whereas an increase in $b$ results in a phase advance. using periodic-orbit waveforms extended over a one-year interval with fixed orbital parameters, we obtain an order-of-magnitude estimate of the sensitivity of the waveform mismatch to nonlocal corrections. for the configurations considered, this estimate suggests sensitivity to $ζ$ of order $10^{-6}$ when $b=2$.

title: going into a tailspin near the abyss: analytic solutions for spinning particles on near equatorial, plunging orbits in kerr spacetime
abstract: this work presents, the first time, analytic solutions for the nearly equatorial, plunging motion of a spinning test-particle in kerr spacetime. the equations of motion are solved at first-order in the small-body spin for all classes of plunging orbits with energy $e < 1$. the solutions incorporate the small precession of the orbital plane caused by the precession of the particle's spin. additionally, we present the correction to the radius of the innermost bound circular orbit in closed form, and introduce a novel, keplerian-like parametrization for generic plunging orbits. our solutions will be useful in the modelling of inspiral-merger-ringdown waveforms with self-force methods and black hole perturbation theory.

title: metric reconstruction for generic black-hole perturbations
abstract: most sourced radiation-gauge reconstructions of kerr perturbations use hertz potentials. we establish the first self-contained newman--penrose transport hierarchy for reconstructing metric perturbations with generic conserved sources on ricci-flat petrov type d backgrounds. in a traceful radiation gauge, two first-order equations determine the trace, after which the total metric follows from an extreme weyl scalar and the prescribed ricci tensor without a hertz potential. we illustrate the method for a schwarzschild black hole with a thin static shell, including a source-supported static completion sector.

title: quasinormal modes and tidal responses of black holes in generic anisotropic matter environments
abstract: we develop a perturbative framework for a black hole embedded in a generic, possibly anisotropic, matter environment under spherical symmetry. our approach extends previous analyses restricted to vanishing radial pressure or to perturbative matter configurations. within this framework, we derive an analytical generalization of the einstein cluster that incorporates a polytropic radial pressure, and we investigate the properties of this solution. we show that both the geodesic structure and the axial quasinormal-mode spectrum remain predominantly governed by an overall gravitational redshift effect, while the radial pressure systematically enhances the environmental corrections. in contrast, the tidal love numbers are substantially more sensitive, and can exhibit order-unity deviations, including vanishing and negative strictly static magnetic love numbers for sufficiently large anisotropy. we present the full linearized equations, which can be applied to various extensions, including ringdown analysis and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals.

title: binary black hole scattering with generic spins
abstract: we study generic-spin black-hole scattering with orbital-plane precession, whose dynamics require more than one scattering angle. from numerical relativity (nr), we extract the polar scattering angle and precession of the orbital plane, the latter characterised by asymptotic euler angles. a dictionary relating post-minkowskian (pm) observables to scattering and euler angles is presented, enabling the first precessing pm-nr comparisons. our results provide a key benchmark for generic-spin resummations and provide the foundations for exploring boundary-to-bound maps in the generic case.

title: static black holes and iyer-wald entropy in $f(\mathcal{r},\mathcal{k})$ gravity
abstract: we investigate static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions in a class of {nonpolynomial} gravitational theories described by a {lagrangian $f=-x^{1-n}$, where $x = \mathcal{r} + \sqrt{6\mathcal{k} - \mathcal{r}^2}$ is a function of the ricci and kretschmann scalars.} the modified einstein equations contain {nonpolynomial} curvature terms. we develop a perturbative scheme to look for a black hole solution that deviates parametrically from the schwarzschild geometry. we obtain first-order corrections to the metric by solving the resulting coupled differential equations. the corresponding iyer--wald entropy is then evaluated consistently to first order in the perturbative coupling. we show that the {nonpolynomial} contribution gives rise to a power-law correction to the bekenstein--hawking entropy.

title: wormhole geometries in extended symmetric teleparallel gravity with $f(q, t) = αq + βt + γt^2$
abstract: in this study, we study static and spherically-symmetric wormhole configurations within the recently proposed class of extended symmetric teleparallel gravities characterised by the functional form $f(q,t)=αq+βt+γt^{2}$, where $q$ is the non-metricity scalar, $t$ is the trace of the energy-momentum tensor, and ($α,β,γ$) are constant coupling parameters. by varying the action with respect to the metric, we derive the modified field equations and cast them in an effective einstein-like form containing additional geometric contributions that depend on $q$ and $t$. we conclude that the $f(q,t)=αq+βt+γt^{2}$ framework offers a viable arena for constructing physically realistic wormholes without invoking severe energy condition violations, opening new pathways for connecting modified gravity phenomenology with astrophysical signatures of non-trivial spacetime topologies.

title: constraining deviations from the teukolsky equation with gw250114
abstract: the recent gravitational-wave detection gw250114 by the ligo-virgo-kagra (lvk) collaboration provides unprecedented precision for testing general relativity (gr) through black hole ringdowns. in this study, we provide the first bounds on theory-agnostic deviations from the teukolsky equation as described by the beyond-teukolsky formalism. it directly connects deviations in the perturbation equations on the level of the effective potential in the teukolsky equation with changes in the quasinormal mode (qnm) spectrum. we incorporate information on the final mass and spin from a full lvk inspiral-merger-ringdown analysis as parametrized priors in our analysis, reflecting theoretical uncertainties. using publicly available lvk posterior information on agnostic damped sinusoid parameters, we then demonstrate how much beyond-teukolsky potentials can be constrained. the high signal-to-noise ratio (snr) allows us to avoid the expensive full bayesian analysis of all parameters and to work directly with a simplified likelihood for the fundamental qnm only. this strategy is promising for future events with even higher snr and allows, in principle, for a quick and simple test of theories beyond gr without performing the full data analysis procedure. we report that current bounds on deviation parameters are in agreement with the teukolsky equation.

title: stability of perturbations around black holes under spatially extended potential deformations
abstract: it has been shown that the spectrum of black hole quasi-normal modes is extremely sensitive to localized deformations of the geometry away from the potential peak. deformations associated with a real astronomical environment may extend over a broad spatial region rather than be localized in a finite region. whether spatially extended fluctuations distributed throughout spacetime can produce similar effects remains unclear. in this work, we construct a toy model to investigate spatially extended effective-potential deformations motivated by geometric or environmental fluctuations. we study how such deformations affect the corresponding perturbation system in the time domain. using both the pöschl-teller and scalar regge-wheeler potentials as representative backgrounds, we show that sufficiently wide oscillatory perturbations of zero mean can drive the corresponding perturbation systems from decay to exponential growth in the time domain. through numerical analysis, we uncover a scaling relation for the instability threshold and further provide an analytical interpretation of its physical origin.

title: two-fluid schwarzschild solution
abstract: \we consider the interior two-fluid schwarzschild solution. that is a model of compact (neutron) stars with admixed dark matter. the two constant energy densities generalize the interior schwarschild solution to the case of two fluids (representing standard model matter and dark matter, for instance), interacting mutually solely by the common gravitational field. in general, the two-fluid core is surrounded by a one-fluid corona (envelope). only for special parameters (the model depends on energy densities $e_1,e_2$ and central pressures $p_{\mathrm{c}1},p_{\mathrm{c}2}$ of the fluids), both fluids occupy the same region. despite the sum of two energy densities in that region, the compactness bound of 4/9 is not exceeded. therefore, a buchdahl limit for two fluids holds. a conceivable object is one with a stark leakage of one fluid (e.g. dark matter) beyond the two-fluid core.

title: spins do not add: why rotating stars do not help spin-up black holes in binaries
abstract: it is well-known that in the merger of a black-hole binary with spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum, the spin of the final black hole always increases with the spin of the components. we show that this very intuitive behavior is violated in black hole--neutron star binaries, where the spin of the final black hole actually decreases as the spin of the neutron star increases. using a large set of binaries with different spins and mass ratios, we identify the mechanism behind this surprising result in the nonlinear dynamics of the tidal disruption, which drives a substantial loss of angular momentum via dynamical ejecta, in some cases comparable to that radiated via gravitational waves. our results highlight that the spin evolution of stellar-mass black holes involved in binary mergers is different from what normally assumed, far more complex, and interesting.

title: the nanograv 15-year data set: a limit on continuous spin gravitons
abstract: continuous spin particles (csps) are massless particles characterized by a dimensionful spin scale, $ρ$, which, when non-zero, changes their helicity under lorentz boosts. since csps reduce to ordinary particles when $ρ\rightarrow 0$, the photon or graviton could be csps and only appear to behave as ordinary particles due to a small value of $ρ$. therefore, it is important to determine what value of $ρ$ is experimentally allowed. recent work has shown that the physical effects of csps scale as powers of $ρ/ω$ when $ρ\ll ω$, where $ω$ is a frequency scale, making low-frequency probes particularly beneficial for highlighting these phenomena. in this paper we use pulsar timing arrays to set constraints on the spin scale of the continuous spin graviton. pulsar timing arrays are uniquely suited for this application as they have exceptional sensitivity to low, nanohertz frequency gravitational waves, as demonstrated by their recent evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. using standard bayesian data analysis techniques, we find that the nanograv 15-year data set constrains the graviton spin scale to $ρ_\text{g} < 1.23 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{ev} $ at the 95% credible level.

title: conic tilings of black hole images by radial closest approach
abstract: each point in a black hole image corresponds to a light ray, whose minimum radial coordinate when traced backward from the observer measures how deeply it probes the spacetime. we show that contours of constant closest-approach radius form arcs of conic sections in standard bardeen image coordinates for kerr, and in natural local image coordinates for finite-radius observers in the broader plebanski-demianski (pd) family of einstein-maxwell solutions. at each radius, the condition of vanishing radial velocity defines a complete conic; the physical contour consists of those points whose rays reach that radius before encountering an outer turning point. for positive killing energy and positive mass, we prove that throughout connected positive-radius regions with positive radial metric function and allowed motion at both endpoints, a local test of the radial potential's slope is sufficient to select the physical arcs. this simplification follows from a coefficient identity imposed by the pd field equations and alignment of the principal null directions. we give explicit counterexamples in a domain crossing r=0 and in the separable ovcharenko-podolsky extension, where an outer turning point invalidates the local test. the conic family also yields a single polynomial equation containing the critical curve in kerr and pd. these results turn the returning image into a geometric map of radial photon propagation, independent of the emission model. (this abstract has been abridged to meet the arxiv character limit.)

title: galilean cosmologies in two dimensions
abstract: inspired by carroll black holes, we consider the most general theory of galilean dilaton gravity in two dimensions. we find generically that the solution space describes cosmological spacetimes. from a limiting perspective, these galilean geometries connect the white and black hole singularities through the bifurcation surface. the latter turns into a galilean extremal surface in the limit of infinite speed of light. we also discuss aspects of galilean tachydynamics and find that the entropy is given by the dilaton evaluated at the galilean extremal surface.

title: ernst-potential driven recovery of kerr with neural networks
abstract: we use artificial neural networks to recover the kerr solution by directly minimizing a regularized ernst sigma-model action. reduction along the axial killing direction avoids the divergence at the ergosphere. compactified coordinates cover the entire black-hole exterior, while the network parametrization enforces the asymptotic data and axis regularity. for dimensionless spins $0.1 \le a/m \le 0.99$, the median maximum relative error in the recovered metric component $g_{ϕϕ}$ remains below $7.2\times10^{-4}$. when only the horizon rod length and angular momentum are prescribed, the networks also predict the mass with median relative errors below $1.8\times10^{-3}$. these results demonstrate the practicality of direct variational training for rotating black-hole geometries.

title: correlation geometry and emergent space-time from stochastic correlation flows
abstract: we propose an effective framework relating correlation geometry to stochastic flows of correlation projectors. physical configurations are encoded by measures on spaces of self-adjoint operators, with physical equivalence defined by unitary conjugation. assuming a smooth, spectrally separated correlation sector, local orthonormal frames define a wilczek--zee connection, while a stratonovich gradient-flow ansatz preserves the projector constraints. in a local continuum approximation with massive fast modes, standard one-loop methods generate yang--mills-type terms and curvature terms of einstein--hilbert form. along a smooth closed path, the trace of a cyclic product of projectors converges to the trace of the parallel-transport operator as the discretization is refined. we examine possible geometric, disordered, and topological regimes and motivate the stochastic dynamics through an effective open-system description. the first-order frame action defines a symplectic structure on the projector sector, providing a starting point for its relation to gravitational canonical variables. we identify the matching conditions required for an ashtekar phase-space description and the assumptions connecting correlation geometry to induced interactions and emergent spacetime.

title: self-gravitating spinning mesonic tubes
abstract: in this paper, we construct new self-gravitating solutions for the four-dimensional $su(2)$ einstein non-linear sigma model and the einstein-skyrme model, both minimally coupled to the maxwell field, which describes spinning pulsed mesonic tubes. these solutions are gyratonic in the sense that they are characterized by a propagation axis and possess angular momentum. the gyratonic solutions are described by a smooth matter distribution, which is free of curvature singularities. the maximum of the energy density is concentrated on a tube around the propagation axis. we first consider the $su(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to general relativity and the maxwell field, constructing asymptotically flat, spinning, pulsed gyratonic solutions. subsequently, we include the skyrme term in the analysis. in this case, we show that in order to maintain the resolvability of the matter field equations, the spacetime must be asymptotically de sitter. it is also shown that, despite the fact that the total topological charge is zero, these solutions possess a non-zero topological charge density.

title: accurate calibration method of the back-linked fabry perot interferometer using null channel for space-based gravitational wave antenna
abstract: accurate calibration of the detector response is essential for precision gravitational-wave (gw) observations. in the back-linked fabry-perot interferometer (blfpi), which employs fabry-perot cavities to achieve high gw sensitivity, accurate calibration of the cavity response is particularly important because residual calibration errors directly limit the suppression of laser frequency noise. however, no practical calibration strategy for the cavity response has yet been established. in this paper, we propose a method for calibrating the cavity response using a null channel constructed from the three interferometer outputs of the triangular laser-link configuration. in null channel, gw signals are canceled and residual laser frequency noise indicates errors in the cavity response estimates. therefore we can estimate the cavity response by optimizing the response parameters to minimize the integrated power of the null channel. we derive the estimation bias introduced by technical noise analytically and evaluate the performance of the proposed method numerically. the results show that the residual laser frequency noise after calibration is more than an order of magnitude below the designed blfpi sensitivity throughout the observation band. this demonstrates that the proposed null-channel calibration method achieves the accuracy required for effective subtraction of laser frequency noise.

title: from matched black-hole scalar charges to gravitational-wave inspirals in a massive scalar--gauss--bonnet effective theory
abstract: massive scalar fields introduce a finite interaction range in scalar--gauss--bonnet (sgb) gravity and can modify the gravitational waves (gws) emitted by binary black holes (bbhs). we develop a matched description that relates the curvature-sourced scalar field of an isolated black hole (bh) to the scalar charge entering the effective binary dynamics. the massive field contains a distributed curvature-forced contribution and a homogeneous yukawa sector. by matching the near- and far-zone solutions, we determine the local static coefficient and derive its finite conversion to a renormalized worldline coupling. the static coefficient has no linear scalar-mass correction, and its first correction is quadratic. we use the leading matched charges in the leading post-newtonian dynamics and gw phasing of nonspinning, quasicircular bbhs while retaining the finite yukawa range and massive-radiation kinematics. the scalar mass modifies the conservative dynamics, produces distinct dipole and quadrupole radiation thresholds, and changes the accumulated inspiral phase. we also construct the associated breathing and longitudinal tidal responses and treat dispersive massive propagation separately. these results connect the finite-mass bh scalar response to source and propagation observables for bbh inspirals.

title: magnetized strange quark matter in hypersurface-homogeneous $f(r,t)$ cosmology: physical closure, isotropization and late-time observational constraints
abstract: cosmological models of magnetized strange quark matter in $f(r,t)$ gravity have so far relied on kinematic ansatzes and lacked observational tests. we revisit them for $f(r,t)=r+2μt$ on a hypersurface-homogeneous background containing the locally rotationally symmetric bianchi i, kantowski--sachs and bianchi iii geometries. treated exactly, the maxwell field couples minimally. because kinematic ansatzes contradict a magnetized source, we close the field equations with the bag-model equation of state and magnetic flux freezing and, adding dust and radiation, solve them exactly in limiting cases and numerically in general. without primordial shear, the field-induced anisotropy keeps, as in general relativity, a nearly constant radiation-era level for $μ\ge0$, then decays as the model approaches de sitter space; an assumed present field of 1 ng leaves $(σ/h)_0\simeq5.8\times10^{-11}$ today. a joint fit to 32 cosmic chronometers, 1590 pantheon+ supernova light curves and baryon acoustic oscillations from the second data release of the dark energy spectroscopic instrument gives $μ=1.12^{+0.65}_{-0.58}$ and $h_0=69.1\pm3.2$~\kmsmpc, and the null, weak and dominant energy conditions hold throughout. relative to the flat $λ$ cold dark matter model, the akaike (aic) and bayesian (bic) information criteria give $δ\mathrm{aic}=-1.4$ and $δ\mathrm{bic}=+4.0$, and the bayes factor is inconclusive. the fitted bag term, $b_c^{1/4}=2.15$ mev, is an effective vacuum energy, not the quantum chromodynamics bag constant. the preference for $μ>0$ depends on the supernova sample and the prior, a constant coupling would shift matter--radiation equality, and the sign of $μ$ depends on the matter lagrangian; $μ$ is therefore an effective late-time parameter.

title: rapidly spinning primordial black holes from confinement
abstract: confinement can turn widely separated particles into rapidly spinning primordial black holes. a flux tube pulls a heavy quark--antiquark pair together, converting its stored energy into relativistic motion. the same mechanism is possible in the magnetic dual, where a higgs phase confines magnetic flux into a string joining a monopole--antimonopole pair. as the particles approach, cosmological tides and string bends can deflect their motion and make them miss. these disturbances can originate during inflation or be generated later. black-hole formation then requires rare close passages from a smooth, broad encounter distribution. the resulting natal spin density therefore rises linearly to extremality, with mean dimensionless spin two thirds. numerical string evolutions recover this law. pairs that miss can remain bound, radiate and later collapse into lighter, near-extremal holes, sourcing a stochastic gravitational-wave background. although the abundance remains model dependent, confinement leaves a unique spin signature that gravitational-wave observations can test.

title: astrometric effects of anisotropic gravitational wave backgrounds
abstract: precise astrometric observations of distant objects such as stars and quasars can be used to probe gravitational wave signals at nanohertz frequencies. a stochastic gravitational wave background (sgwb) produces correlated apparent motions of pairs of objects on the sky. that correlation as a function of their angular separation is the astrometric analog of the hellings-downs curve in the context of pulsar timing measurements. upper limits on the sgwb have been obtained from very-long baseline interferometry and gaia astrometry, and future gaia data releases are expected to improve them. an astrophysical background from inspiraling supermassive black hole binaries is expected to be significantly anisotropic. in this work, we compute the astrometric correlation functions for an anisotropic sgwb, known as the generalized overlap reduction functions, for all six gravitational wave polarizations. we present closed-form expressions in all cases where the distant-light source limit can be applied, following the approach used for pulsar timing arrays. we find that the correlations differ qualitatively between the tensor, vector, and scalar polarizations. finally, we discuss the applicability of these results in future astrometry searches for arbitrarily polarized anisotropic gravitational wave backgrounds.

title: quasinormal modes of a black hole in a dehnen-type dark matter halo with radial pressure
abstract: we investigate the quasinormal modes (qnms) of scalar and (axial) gravitational perturbations of a black hole spacetime surrounded by a dehnen-type dark matter (dm) halo with nonvanishing radial pressure. our results reveal that the real and imaginary parts of the qnms exhibit distinct redshift coefficients with respect to the dm halo compactness $m/a_0$, in contrast to the vanishing radial pressure case. the magnitude of this effect is dominated by the profile parameter $γ$, and the damping rate is more sensitive to the dm halo compactness than the oscillation frequency. in the eikonal limit, the redshift deviations are well captured by the light ring angular velocity $ω_c$ and the lyapunov exponent $λ$.

title: foort: flexible object-oriented ray tracing
abstract: we present foort (flexible object-oriented ray tracing), an open c++ code for ray-tracing images of black holes and other compact objects in arbitrary spacetimes. foort is designed to offer flexibility and can handle horizons, naked singularities and numerical metrics, allowing it to ray-trace numerous different metrics including kerr and other black holes, as well as horizonless objects such as fuzzballs and boson stars. new metrics, analytical or numerical, can be added with minimal effort, and geodesics are initialized at the camera without reference to conserved quantities, so no special structure of the metric is required. besides the intensity observed from a geometrically and optically thin equatorial disk, foort is set up to track a number of diagnostics along each geodesic, such as the number of equatorial crossings and the radius of closest approach. its adaptive mesh can refine the image on any of these diagnostics, efficiently resolving narrow features such as higher-order photon rings. accompanying python tools convert the output into images and interferometric visibility amplitudes. we describe the main features of the code, validate it against analytic results in the schwarzschild and kerr spacetimes, demonstrate it on several non-kerr metrics, and characterize its scaling with the number of openmp threads. foort is lightweight, requiring only c++17 and openmp, and has already been used in a number of studies of black hole and compact-object imaging. the code is publicly available in a github repository.

title: maximal force bounds in general relativity and beyond
abstract: gibbons and schiller proposed the maximal force conjecture in general relativity, according to which the maximum force is bounded by $c^4/g$. in this work, we derive upper bounds on the force for stable, self-gravitating, spatially regular and horizonless compact objects in $d$-dimensional general relativity, braneworld gravity, pure lovelock gravity and einstein-gauss-bonnet gravity. our analysis uses the connection between photon-ring structure and the stability of horizonless compact objects, adopting the absence of light rings as a criterion for stability. we investigate how the resulting force bounds depend on the spacetime dimension and on modifications to gravitational dynamics arising from extra dimensions and higher curvature corrections. we study how the bounds for such systems change under alternative higher curvature theories of gravity or in higher dimensions. throughout this work, we consider a static and spherically symmetric spacetime sourced by anisotropic matter for which the radial and tangential pressures may differ.

title: slow macroscopic rotations of neutron stars with a deformed effective surface
abstract: the macroscopic model for a neutron star (ns) as a finite perfect fluid at the equilibrium is extended to rotating deformed systems by incorporating the linear perturbation expansion over a small frequency $ω$ near the schwarzschild gravitational metric within the effective-surface (es) approach. the ns angular momentum $i$ and moment of inertia (mi) for a slow stationary azimuthal rotation around the symmetry axis is calculated by using the kerr metric approach in spheroidal coordinates, and compared with the spherical results. the gradient surface terms of the macroscopic ns energy density $\mathcal{e}(ρ)$ (equation of state) are taken into account along with the volume ones at the leading order of the leptodermic parameter $a/r \ll 1$, where $a$ is the es crust thickness and $r$ is the ns effective radius. the analytical macroscopic ns mi expressions, $θ= di/dω= \widetildeθ/(1-\mathcal{t}_{tφ})$, have been obtained in terms of the statistically averaged mi, $\tildeθ$, and its time and azimuthal-angle $t,φ$ correlation, $\mathcal{t}_{tφ}$, as sums of the volume and surface components. the mi $θ$ is changed significantly as function of the effective radius $r$ and deformation parameter because of a strong gravity. we found the additional narrower constraints for the ns radius due mainly to the $t,φ$ correlations and surface contributions and ns surface deformation. the adiabaticity conditions for application of the linear perturbation theory is carried out for several neutron stars with a strong gravity and relatively large rotation periods.

title: exact transformation-optics representation of the ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
abstract: we derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. an orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured euclidean chart with refractive index $n(ρ)=1+a^2/(4ρ^2)$. through the plebański correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=μ_r=n(ρ)\,\mathbb{1}$ and its full vector-maxwell operator. for the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through jost solutions and wronskians. nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|r_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. the reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. this theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. we compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|t_l|^2\propto(ωa/c)^{4l+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $l=1,2,3,4$. the transmission cross section tends to $πa^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. we also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive lorentz model. the constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.

title: highly spinning binary black holes: promise and pitfalls for parameterized tests of general relativity
abstract: highly spinning binary black holes exhibit complex inspiral dynamics and offer a powerful opportunity to probe gravity in a stronger-field and more dynamical regime than non-spinning binaries. gravitational-wave signals from such systems enable stringent parameterized tests of deviations from the source dynamics predicted by general relativity. we show that highly spinning, mass-asymmetric binaries can provide enhanced sensitivity to deviations entering at higher post-newtonian orders, which remain comparatively poorly constrained. using nr simulations from the sxs catalog, we first recover the injected signals within general relativity using $\texttt{imrphenomxphm-spintaylor}$, $\texttt{imrphenomxpnr}$, and $\texttt{seobnrv5phm}$, finding model-dependent biases in the inferred masses, spins, and spin orientations. we then analyze the same signals with the $\texttt{imrphenomxphm}$-based inspiral parameterized test of general relativity framework, tiger, and find that these waveform-systematic biases can lead to apparent deviations from general relativity, which become significant for loud signals. our results highlight that highly spinning binaries offer powerful tests of higher-order post-newtonian deviations, but waveform inaccuracies can lead to false signs of new physics.

title: eccentricity detectability in extreme mass-ratio inspirals
abstract: extreme mass-ratio inspirals (emris) consist of a stellar-mass compact object orbiting a massive black hole and are among the primary targets for the future space-based gravitational-wave detector lisa. their orbital eccentricity carries valuable information about their astrophysical origins, making its detection particularly important. however, increasing eccentricity has competing effects on detectability: it makes eccentric waveforms easier to distinguish from circular ones, but also redistributes signal power across multiple harmonics, reducing the power captured by single-harmonic searches. in this work, we quantify this trade-off within a semi-coherent framework for a source with fixed total snr of $50$. eccentricity becomes distinguishable from zero for final eccentricities $e_f \gtrsim 0.05$, while single-harmonic sensitivity declines beyond $e_f \simeq 0.1$. in noise-free analyses, including enough harmonics to recover at least $50\%$ of the total snr avoids this degradation, but adds statistical freedom when calibrating detection thresholds. we apply the framework to two astrophysical emri populations, showing how these competing effects interact with their eccentricity distributions under simplified assumptions. the balance among eccentricity-driven distinguishability, harmonic power loss, and the statistical cost of additional harmonics is an important consideration for future emri search developments.

title: einstein reconstruction scheme: metric reconstruction by direct inversion of the einstein operator
abstract: we propose a metric reconstruction scheme that computes the metric directly from the linearized einstein equations for noncompact sources. working in a traceful radiation gauge, we hierarchically solve four einstein transport equations, with the remaining six enforced by suitable homogeneous data. unlike previous newman-penrose approaches, we show how the homogeneous data are fixed, thereby closing the full set of einstein equations. we conclude by relating our scheme to existing sourced reconstruction methods, thus establishing a connection between the newman-penrose and hertz-potential approaches.

title: cosmological correlators and kinematic flow on complex hartle-hawking saddles
abstract: the lorentzian gravitational path integral over homogeneous and isotropic metrics in a closed universe with positive cosmological constant is dominated by complex saddle points, such as the hartle-hawking saddles. we ask how to compute cosmological correlators on such complex backgrounds, and how they respond to the shifts of the kinematic variables---the kinematic flow---without tracking the bulk time evolution explicitly. we, specifically, study a conformally coupled scalar test field with a cubic interaction around these saddles. we find that the wave function coefficients can be written as discrete spectral sums with the summands containing the corresponding coefficients in the einstein static universe, which are obtainable in analogy with the polytopes program for flat spacetime. whereas the wave function coefficients of the flat flrw case are given by integrals over shifted kinematics, the discrete spectrum on the three-sphere for hartle-hawking saddles produces sums. we identify the coefficients, which depend on the final hypersurface through a phase fixed by its size, with srivastava-daoust multi-variable hypergeometric functions. they satisfy recursion relations for any number of sites, under which the sums collapse into rational functions. for the one- and two-site feynman-witten tree diagrams, we derive difference equations in the kinematic variables which close on a finite set of sums, giving a discrete kinematic flow. the transformation matrices are upper triangular with rational elements, and satisfy a consistency condition which makes the flow path independent. we then obtain the two-, three- and four-point cosmological correlators. at the late-time conformal boundary, we derive an explicit difference equation for the four-point function.

title: cubic curvature deformations to the kerr black hole shadow
abstract: we investigate the effects of cubic curvature corrections on the shadows of rotating black holes within the effective field theory of gravity. starting from a perturbatively corrected kerr metric incorporating two independent cubic curvature couplings, we construct black hole shadows through numerical integration of null geodesics, without assuming separability of the geodesic equations. using a hamiltonian ray-tracing approach, we systematically examine the dependence of the shadow geometry on the higher-curvature couplings, black hole spin, and observer inclination. we find that cubic curvature interactions can produce discernible deviations from the kerr shadow, modifying its apparent size and shape. in particular, the two cubic interactions exhibit distinct effects on the shadow boundary, with the magnitude of the deviations depending sensitively on the coupling strengths and black hole spin. we validate our numerical results through independent convergence tests of the geodesic integration and shadow-boundary determination, and recover the analytical kerr shadow in the vanishing-coupling limit. our results provide a complementary probe of higher-curvature gravity in the strong-field regime and illustrate the potential of black hole shadow observations to constrain departures from general relativity.
